text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Finance Minister Paul Martin rules out major tax cuts: Despite success in lowering deficit, minister stresses need to continue restraint.
- Liberals, Reform courting taxpayers: Parties may seek votes by sharing the spoils.
- Ministers must be seen to do right thing: Secret rules limit right to lobby.
- Top court rejects integration as a right: Schools for disabled not a violation.
- British Columbia urges abortion-pill action: Province says drug would cut costs, help pregnant teens.
- Canadian Auto Workers walkout closes all General Motors Canada's plants: Nearly 6,000 workers join strike as talks continue to falter.
- Manulife chasing Altamira: Mutual fund firm owners said to be negotiating in renewed attempt to complete deal.
- Finance Minister Paul Martin's statement boosts bonds: Reaction bodes well for interest rates.
- Rogers sells cable clusters: Cogeco to pay about C$350 million for 300,000 subscribers.
- Talks on freeing up power sales zapped: Ontario, Quebec lead opposition.
- 'Free-for-all' as Quebec nickel-copper rush is on.

- Finance Minister Paul Martin rejects tax cut: Says Ottawa beat its deficit target by C$4.1 billion last year but he sets aggressive new deficit-reduction goals instead of using the cushion to lower taxes.
